claim: In an \(n\)-firm homogeneous-good Cournot game with constant marginal costs \(c_i\ge 0\) and a common continuous strictly decreasing inverse-demand function \(P(Q)\) satisfying \(\lim_{Q\to\infty}P(Q)=0\), every interior Cournot equilibrium is bankruptcy-free if and only if all firms have the same marginal cost.
integrity: Illustrative arithmetic is explicit; no numerical experiment is used as proof.
A plausible primary source full text was inaccessible, leaving a stated overlap risk.
scientific_limitations: Interior equilibria only; inactive firms are not classified.
Homogeneous good, common continuous strictly decreasing inverse demand, constant nonnegative marginal costs.
No claim about repeated-game equilibrium supportability.
title: Bankruptcy-free Cournot equilibrium is equivalent to equal active costs
